title: Atopic Dermatitis Endpoints in FDA Approvals Since 2017: IGA 0/1, EASI-75 and Itch NRS in Systemic vs Topical Products
summary: The primary and key secondary endpoints behind FDA atopic dermatitis approvals since 2017, with systemic and topical products compared on IGA 0/1, EASI-75 and itch NRS.
body_markdown:
## Atopic dermatitis endpoints behind FDA approvals since 2017: IGA 0/1, EASI-75 and itch NRS in systemic vs topical products


### Key takeaways


- **The IGA responder endpoint is the constant.** Every systemic and topical atopic dermatitis (AD) label reviewed uses an investigator global assessment of clear (0) or almost clear (1). In almost every program this also requires at least a 2-grade improvement from baseline, and it is the primary or co-primary endpoint. The instrument varies (IGA, ISGA, vIGA-AD), but the responder definition is essentially the same[433](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=595f437d-2729-40bb-9c62-c8ece1f82780)[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=238)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242)[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=256)[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=274)[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=339)[442](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=9309d20f-8cd4-4c96-93fa-7f730e83c7ab)[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=328) .
- **Systemic products usually add EASI-75 as a co-primary endpoint.** Tralokinumab (Adbry), abrocitinib (Cibinqo), upadacitinib (Rinvoq) and nemolizumab (Nemluvio) used IGA 0/1 plus EASI-75 as co-primaries[287](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=287)[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=238)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242)[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=300) . Dupilumab (Dupixent) and lebrikizumab (Ebglyss) used IGA 0/1 with at least a 2-point improvement as the sole primary, and reported EASI-75 as an additional endpoint[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=206)[203](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=203) .
- **Topical products rely on a single IGA-success primary endpoint over a shorter window.** Their labels generally do not report EASI-75. Timepoints are Day 29 (crisaborole), Week 4 (roflumilast cream, difamilast) or Week 8 (ruxolitinib cream, tapinarof)[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=256)[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=339)[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=328)[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=274)[442](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=9309d20f-8cd4-4c96-93fa-7f730e83c7ab) . Systemic trials measured at Week 16, or Week 12 for most abrocitinib trials[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=233)[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=238) .
- **Itch NRS response is the standard key secondary endpoint.** It is almost always defined as a ≥4-point improvement on a 0 to 10 scale and analyzed only in patients with a baseline score of at least 4. Systemic programs report it in all age groups studied. Topical programs report it only in patients aged 12 and older, and some topical labels (crisaborole, difamilast) report no itch endpoint at all[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=233)[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=282)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242)[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=274)[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=339)[443](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=9309d20f-8cd4-4c96-93fa-7f730e83c7ab)[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=255)[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=362) .


### Products covered


This overview covers FDA-labeled AD products with an approval or efficacy supplement on or after January 1, 2017. Eucrisa's original approval (December 14, 2016) predates that window; it qualifies through its 2020 and 2023 efficacy supplements (Drugs@FDA, NDA 207695).


Route / class Product (application) Labeled AD population in pivotal program

### Systemic products: endpoint architecture and results


#### Common design features


Systemic pivotal trials enrolled moderate-to-severe patients with near-identical entry criteria: IGA ≥3, EASI ≥16 and ≥10% BSA involvement[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=206)[287](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=287)[203](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=203)[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=300) . Abrocitinib, upadacitinib and nemolizumab also required a baseline itch score of at least 4 at entry[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=238)[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=252)[380](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=380) . Most programs ran paired monotherapy trials plus a trial with concomitant topical corticosteroids (TCS). Rescue therapy or missing data were imputed as nonresponse[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=233)[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=290)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242) .


#### Primary endpoints and Week 16 (or Week 12) results, drug vs placebo


Product Primary endpoint(s) Monotherapy results With TCS results


Dupixent 300 mg Q2W IGA 0/1 + ≥2-point improvement, Wk 16 (EASI-75 as other endpoint)[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=206) SOLO 1: 38% vs 10%; SOLO 2: 36% vs 9%[433](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=595f437d-2729-40bb-9c62-c8ece1f82780) CHRONOS: 39% vs 12%[433](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=595f437d-2729-40bb-9c62-c8ece1f82780)


Adbry 300 mg Q2W Co-primary IGA 0/1 and EASI-75, Wk 16[287](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=287) ECZTRA 1: IGA 16% vs 7%, EASI-75 25% vs 13%; ECZTRA 2: IGA 21% vs 9%, EASI-75 33% vs 10%[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=290) ECZTRA 3: IGA 38% vs 27%, EASI-75 56% vs 37%[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=290)


Ebglyss 250 mg Q2W IGA 0/1 + ≥2-point improvement, Wk 16 (EASI-75, EASI-90, itch as other outcomes)[203](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=203) ADvocate 1: 43% vs 13%; ADvocate 2: 33% vs 11%[196](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=196) ADhere: the label says only that results were consistent with the monotherapy trials; no figures given[199](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=199)


Nemluvio 30 mg Q4W Co-primary IGA success (0/1 + ≥2-point) and EASI-75, Wk 16[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=300) Not studied as monotherapy[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=300) ARCADIA 1: IGA 36% vs 25%, EASI-75 44% vs 29%; ARCADIA 2: IGA 38% vs 26%, EASI-75 42% vs 30%[301](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=301)


Cibinqo 200 mg / 100 mg QD Co-primary IGA 0/1 + ≥2-grade and EASI-75, Wk 12[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=238) AD-1: IGA 44%/24% vs 8%, EASI-75 62%/40% vs 12%; AD-2: IGA 38%/28% vs 9%, EASI-75 61%/44% vs 10%[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=323) AD-3 (adults): IGA 47%/36% vs 14%, EASI-75 68%/58% vs 27%[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=323) ; AD-4 (adolescents): IGA 46%/39% vs 24%, EASI-75 71%/64% vs 41%[319](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=319)


Rinvoq 30 mg / 15 mg QD Co-primary vIGA-AD 0/1 + ≥2-grade and EASI-75, Wk 16[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242) AD-1: vIGA 62%/48% vs 8%, EASI-75 80%/70% vs 16%; AD-2: vIGA 52%/39% vs 5%, EASI-75 73%/60% vs 13%[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=241) AD-3: vIGA 59%/40% vs 11%, EASI-75 77%/65% vs 26%[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=251)


Two design points matter for comparing programs. First, the Adbry label defines IGA response as IGA 0/1 and does not state a separate ≥2-grade improvement requirement[287](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=287) . Second, placebo response rises when patients use background TCS. In ECZTRA 3 the placebo + TCS IGA rate was 27%, and across both ARCADIA trials (all patients on TCS/TCI) it was 25 to 26%[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=290)[301](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=301) . The corresponding placebo rates in monotherapy trials were in the single digits or low teens[433](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=595f437d-2729-40bb-9c62-c8ece1f82780)[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=323)[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=241) .


#### Key secondary endpoints in systemic programs


**Itch NRS ≥4-point response (Week 16 unless stated), drug vs placebo:**


- Dupixent (weekly averaged Peak Pruritus NRS, baseline ≥4 subgroup): SOLO 1 41% vs 12%; SOLO 2 36% vs 10%; CHRONOS 59% vs 20%[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=233)[207](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=207) .
- Adbry (weekly average Worst Daily Pruritus NRS, a secondary endpoint): ECZTRA 1 20% vs 10%; ECZTRA 2 25% vs 9%; ECZTRA 3 46% vs 35%[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=282)[285](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=285) .
- Ebglyss (Pruritus NRS, 0 to 10): ADvocate 1 46% vs 13%; ADvocate 2 40% vs 12%[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=195)[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=202) .
- Nemluvio (PP-NRS, explicitly the key secondary endpoint): ARCADIA 1 33% vs 15%; ARCADIA 2 36% vs 15%[302](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=302)[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=300) .
- Rinvoq (Worst Pruritus NRS, assessed at Weeks 1, 4 and 16): at Week 16, 30 mg / 15 mg vs placebo was 60%/52% vs 12% (AD-1), 60%/42% vs 9% (AD-2) and 64%/52% vs 15% (AD-3 with TCS). The label shows the Week 1 and Week 4 results graphically only[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=241)[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=251)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242) .
- Cibinqo (PP-NRS4, early timepoint): at Week 2, 200 mg / 100 mg vs placebo was 28%/11% vs 2% (AD-1), 24%/11% vs 2% (AD-2), 30%/14% vs 8% (AD-3) and 25%/13% vs 8% (AD-4). The label describes a Week 12 benefit without giving percentages[395](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=3f6d6fcd-e9f9-42c8-bfa2-bb2cfc9ed258)[399](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=3f6d6fcd-e9f9-42c8-bfa2-bb2cfc9ed258) .


**Deeper skin clearance and other patient-reported outcomes:**


- EASI-90: Dupixent 36% vs 8% (SOLO 1), 30% vs 7% (SOLO 2) and 40% vs 11% (CHRONOS)[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=233) . Ebglyss 38% vs 9% and 31% vs 10%[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=195) .
- Rinvoq reports both EASI-90 and EASI-100 as secondary endpoints. In AD-1, EASI-90 was 66%/53% vs 8% and EASI-100 was 27%/17% vs 2%[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=241)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242) .
- Rinvoq also reports a skin-pain NRS ≥4-point response in the monotherapy trials: 63%/54% vs 15% in AD-1[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242) .
- Ebglyss reports maintenance of EASI-75 at Week 52 among Week 16 responders[201](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=201) . Dupixent reports maintenance of IGA 0/1 at Week 36 in SOLO CONTINUE (53% on continued dupilumab vs 10% on placebo)[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=221) .


#### Pediatric systemic extensions


Pediatric programs kept the adult endpoint set. Dupixent in adolescents (AD-1526) showed IGA 0/1 + ≥2-point improvement of 24% vs 2%, EASI-75 of 42% vs 8% and Peak Pruritus NRS ≥4-point response of 37% vs 5%[218](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=218) . In children aged 6 months to 5 years on concomitant TCS (AD-1539), the Dupixent primary endpoint was IGA 0/1 without a stated ≥2-point improvement requirement (28% vs 4%). This trial used a Worst Scratch/Itch NRS rather than a patient-rated pruritus NRS (48% vs 9%)[208](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=208) . Adbry's adolescent trial (ECZTRA 6) used co-primary IGA 0/1 and EASI-75 (21% vs 4% and 29% vs 6%) and an Adolescent Worst Pruritus NRS secondary endpoint (23% vs 3%)[293](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=293)[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=288) .


### Topical products: endpoint architecture and results


#### Common design features


Topical pivotal trials were vehicle-controlled, usually randomized 2:1, and run as monotherapy[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=256)[391](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=391)[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=328) . Most enrolled mild-to-moderate disease (IGA 2 to 3) and set BSA caps: 3 to 20% for ruxolitinib cream, 5 to 40% for difamilast and 5 to 95% treatable BSA for crisaborole[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=274)[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=328)[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=256) . Tapinarof is the exception. Its ADORING program enrolled moderate-to-severe patients (87% moderate) with a mean baseline EASI of 12.9[391](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=391) . Pediatric patients were a large share of topical programs. For example, 86% of crisaborole subjects and 80% of tapinarof subjects were aged 2 to 17[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=256)[391](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=391) .


#### Primary endpoints and results, drug vs vehicle


Product Primary endpoint and timepoint Results


Eucrisa 2% ointment BID ISGA success (0/1 + ≥2-grade), Day 29[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=256) Trial 1: 32.8% vs 25.4%; Trial 2: 31.4% vs 18.0%[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=256)

#### Key secondary endpoints in topical programs


- **Opzelura:** Itch NRS (7-day average of worst itch in the prior 24 hours) ≥4-point reduction at Week 8, in patients aged ≥12 with baseline ≥4. Results were 52.2% vs 15.4% (TRuE-AD1) and 50.7% vs 16.3% (TRuE-AD2). The label reports no itch data for the 2 to 11 year trial[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=274)[402](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=24da5509-6631-4795-9d42-273faecd08e7) .
- **Zoryve:** Secondary endpoints were vIGA-AD success at Weeks 1 and 2, and Worst Itch NRS success (≥4-point reduction, patients ≥12 with baseline ≥4) at Weeks 1, 2 and 4. Week 4 itch results were 33.6% vs 20.7% (INTEGUMENT-1) and 30.2% vs 12.4% (INTEGUMENT-2). The Week 1 vIGA-AD difference in INTEGUMENT-2 was not statistically significant[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=339)[337](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=337) . The 2 to 5 year trial had only early vIGA-AD secondary endpoints[333](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=333) .
- **Vtama:** PP-NRS ≥4-point reduction at Week 8 in patients ≥12 with baseline ≥4 was 56% vs 34% (ADORING 1) and 53% vs 24% (ADORING 2). These vehicle itch responses are notably high[443](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=9309d20f-8cd4-4c96-93fa-7f730e83c7ab) .
- **Eucrisa and Adquey:** The labels report no itch NRS, EASI or other secondary efficacy results[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=255)[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=362) . Eucrisa shows ISGA success over time (Days 8 to 29) graphically only[262](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=262) .

### Regulatory context and open questions


FDA's AD-specific guidance, *Atopic Dermatitis: Timing of Pediatric Studies During Development of Systemic Drugs* (final, October 2018), addresses when to include pediatric age groups, including children under 2 years, and says FDA will address technical aspects of pediatric AD development in a future guidance. It does not define IGA success, EASI thresholds or itch NRS responder criteria[420](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=420)[421](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=421) . The label precedents above are therefore the main public reference for endpoint selection.


Three questions remain open for sponsors:


- **Which itch instrument to use.** The labels use Peak Pruritus, Worst Pruritus, Worst Daily Pruritus and Worst Itch NRS, plus observer-reported scratch/itch scales for young children. This variation limits comparison across programs[207](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=207)[285](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=285)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=242)[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=339)[208](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=208) .
- **How to handle high vehicle itch responses in topical trials.** One example is the 34% vehicle rate in ADORING 1[443](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=9309d20f-8cd4-4c96-93fa-7f730e83c7ab) .
- **What evidence is needed to support EASI-based labeling claims for topical products.** No topical label reviewed reports EASI-75[401](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=24da5509-6631-4795-9d42-273faecd08e7)[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=339)[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/atopic-dermatitis-endpoints-behind-fda-approvals?showSourceNumber=362) .
